start.inline.hint: It is type-checked as strict TypeScript (the first level's compile step). Wrap it in an IIFE; give elements a type and use ?. on them. For bundled JS, tick "Skip the type check" (it puts // @ts-nocheck on line 1). Write import '{' z '}' from "zod" as the first statement to use Zod (not available with "Before navigation"). A variable declared with const '{' query '}' = defineParams(z.object('{' … '}')) gets a field under "Per-crawl values". export cannot be written (compile stops it with BH0006: in a page it is a syntax error, and nothing would run). With "After load", your script runs at its place in the numbered order of the scripts (at the top to begin with); with "Before navigation", it runs before all the others. The name of the script (after inline-) starts with a lowercase letter and holds lowercase letters, digits and -, up to 57 characters. The name with inline- in front becomes the id of this script.

trace.notes.clocks: The bars (steps, details, console) are placed by BrowserHive's clock, and the request marks by Chromium's clock. They are separate clocks and can differ a little.
trace.notes.recordedAt: The "Did not finish", "Failed", "Denied" and "Not archived" marks sit at the time they were recorded. That is not the start of the request (a request that did not finish sits at the time recording stopped).
trace.notes.unobservable: The documents of cross-site frames and the scripts of dedicated workers count as "Did not finish", because their end cannot be observed.
trace.notes.unsigned: This view lays out what it read from the .result.json in the store and from the WACZ, and the signature does not cover it. The records to show as evidence are the ones inside the WACZ.

trace.noLength.pending: it had not finished when the capture was stopped
trace.noLength.unobservable: its end event does not reach the captured page's side
trace.noLength.policy: what the response said in an exchange we decided not to keep is not written to the line
trace.noLength.evicted: too many requests were in flight, so it was no longer tracked
trace.noLength.failed: the time of the failure did not arrive
trace.timing.otherMs: Other (queued before sending; held by BrowserHive)
trace.notes.traceAxis: The request bars are drawn from the lines BrowserHive put in its answer (the trace). A start is placed on the same axis as the step bars, and a length includes the time BrowserHive held the request and the response.
trace.notes.traceUnobservable: "End not observable" is not a request that failed to finish: its end event does not reach the captured page's side (the document of a cross-site frame, the script of a dedicated worker). It has no length and is not counted as "Did not finish".
trace.notes.traceUnsigned: This view lays out what it read from the .result.json in the store, and it is not under the signature. The lines are not inside the WACZ. What stands as the record is what is inside the WACZ.
